source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Durian fruit borer (Conogethes punctiferalis) is one of the pests specifically named as a major fruit-damaging pest in durian production, consistent with its description in Source A of this batch. The moth lays eggs on the fruit surface, and the hatching caterpillar bores into the fruit, feeding on the flesh and seed, leaving an entry hole with visible frass. Damaged fruit is unmarketable and should be removed and destroyed to break the pest's life cycle rather than left to fall and decompose near the tree. General control approach: regular orchard inspection to catch and remove infested fruit early, keeping fruit from touching each other on the cluster (reduces egg-laying sites), and insecticide treatment during the vulnerable young-fruit window where infestation pressure is historically high in a given orchard; specific product/rate recommendations should be confirmed locally.
